Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

reverse noun

the opposite

also the reverse, the opposite, contrary, the contrary, on the contrary, quite the reverse, the other way round, in reverse, backwards

classical

Cic. Tusc. 4.34: hujus virtūtis contrāria est vitiōsitās (Lewis & Short)
Caes. BG 7.30: ex contrāriō (Lewis & Short)

contrārium, contrāriī n.

noun, second declension

the opposite, the reverse

The neuter of contrārius, opposite, which takes a genitive or a dative. Ex contrāriō (Nepos ē contrāriō) is “on the contrary, conversely”; in contrārium, into the reverse.

Other words

  • contrā — on the contrary, the other way

    adverb · also used · classical · Cic. Tusc. 4.84 (Lewis & Short)

    Sets one clause against another; as an answer that denies what was said, immō (see actually).

  • retrō — backwards, in reverse (of movement)

    adverb · also used · classical · Liv. 30.10: retrō inhibitā nāve (Lewis & Short)

    For going backwards, as a car in reverse: retrō agere, to drive it back.

Examples

  • Immō contrā: ille mē pulsāvit, nōn ego illum.

    No, the other way round: he hit me, not I him.composed

See also actually, contrast, different, opposite.
